materialParse.title: Material description reader
materialParse.value: Turns free-text material descriptions into composition, weight and width.
materialParse.what: Reads each material's description and fills structured fields: fibre composition, recycled content, construction, weight, width and content class. Results are shown for review before they are saved to the material master.

needs.1: Nothing new: uses the material master's descriptions

importFix.title: Import fix suggestions
importFix.value: Suggests the right code for blocked import rows.
importFix.what: When a workbook row is blocked (unknown customer, unit, material or product type), suggests the matching code from the reference lists, with how sure it is.

needs.1: Nothing new: uses the import's issues and the reference lists

conceptMatch.title: Concept to existing styles
conceptMatch.value: Finds proven styles to start a new concept from.
conceptMatch.what: From a Concept Studio brief, finds the closest existing styles (product type, fabric, trims, price) and explains why, so a new concept can start from a proven BOM.

needs.1: Nothing new: uses Concept Studio briefs and the library's BOMs

lookAlike.title: Look-alike search
lookAlike.value: Upload a photo, find similar styles in the library.
lookAlike.what: Compares pictures: upload a photo or sketch (a competitor sample, a buyer's reference) and get the most similar styles in the library by silhouette, panels and details.

needs.1: Photos or sketches on most styles
needs.2: An image embedding model on the in-house AI server
needs.3: Vector search in SQL Server 2025 (built-in VECTOR type, no new database)

techPack.title: Tech pack reader
techPack.value: Reads a customer tech pack PDF into BOM lines.
techPack.what: Reads a customer tech pack (PDF) and turns its BOM pages into import rows: parts, materials, consumption and units, with a confidence per row; uncertain rows are marked for review in the import preview.

needs.1: Sample tech packs from each customer
needs.2: A document-reading model on the in-house AI server
needs.3: A mapping review with merchandisers for each customer's layout

colorway.title: Colour reader
colorway.value: Reads a colorway photo into named colours.
colorway.what: Reads the main colours from a colorway photo, with their share of the garment and the nearest colour in the customer's colour library.

needs.2: The customers' colour libraries (code, name, reference colour)

costPredict.title: Cost estimate from BOM
costPredict.value: Estimates FOB from a BOM before costing.
costPredict.what: Estimates the FOB of a new style from its BOM, product type and the closest quoted styles, with a range and the main cost drivers.

needs.1: Quotation history linked to the library's styles (Garment Quotation moved onto the new tables)

leadTime.title: Lead-time forecast
leadTime.value: Forecasts production lead time and its risks.
leadTime.what: Forecasts the lead time of a style from its materials, nominated suppliers and factory, and names the longest path and the risks.

needs.1: Actual lead times from production (the SBU lead-time source fixed first)

assistant.title: Library assistant
assistant.value: Ask questions about the library in plain words.
assistant.what: A chat that answers questions about styles, BOMs and changes by running the library's own searches and checks (read-only), and shows which ones it ran.

needs.1: The in-house AI server with a model that can call tools
needs.2: A read-only list of the procedures it may call, with the user's own access rights

materials.title: Materials
materials.subtitle: Every material on a BOM and how widely it is used. Open one to see every style that uses it, its usual consumption per product type, its suppliers and colours.
materials.scopedHint: Counts cover only the styles of the chosen customer and season.

unusual.low: Much lower than usual for this product type
unusual.high: Much higher than usual for this product type

materials.firstUses: Showing the newest {{ shown }} of {{ total }} BOM lines.
materials.consumptionHint: How much of this material a style uses, per product type (brand consumption, else LCO, totalled per style). Use it to sanity-check a new BOM.
materials.rangeLabel: From {{ min }} to {{ max }} {{ uom }}, usual {{ median }}
materials.consumptionLegend: Line: lowest to highest. Box: the middle half of the styles. Mark: the usual (median) value. Uses under 0.6× or over 1.6× the usual value are flagged in Where used.
materials.noConsumption: No consumption recorded for this material.
materials.multiSupplier: Bought from {{ count }} sources. Check whether prices and lead times match.
materials.similarHint: Materials with the same description, or the same code before the "_" version suffix. They may be one material entered twice; check before ordering or merging.
materials.noSimilar: No other material looks like this one.

hint.trims: Trims, accessories, labels and packaging used on this product type, by share of its styles. Many different materials doing the same job (several used only once) is a chance to standardise and cut minimums.
hint.suppliers: How styles and materials are spread across SAP suppliers. Materials only one supplier provides are a sourcing risk; lines without a supplier need one.
hint.duplicates: Materials whose descriptions are identical (ignoring case and spaces). Some are one material entered under several codes; others share a generic description (e.g. "ADDITIONAL LABEL"). Check before merging.
hint.recycled: Share of fabric lines whose description says recycled (RECYCLED, REC., PET-REC, Primegreen), and styles whose fabrics are all recycled.
hint.colours: The most used material colours. Colours under several codes may be the same colour coded differently.

bandHint.standard: On half or more of the styles: the default for a new style of this type.
bandHint.occasional: On fewer than 20% of the styles (the 150 most used are listed).

ins.supplierScope: {{ styles }} styles · {{ materials }} materials · {{ lines }} BOM lines in scope.
ins.dupTotals: {{ groups }} groups covering {{ materials }} materials. Groups used on the most styles come first.
ins.dupGroup: {{ count }} codes · {{ styles }} styles in total
ins.dupFirst: Showing the first {{ shown }} of {{ total }} groups. Filter by section to see others.
ins.allRecycledStyles: {{ count }} of {{ styles }} styles all recycled
ins.recycledRule: Read from BOM descriptions, so a fabric is counted only when its description says so. Seasons without any (e.g. Skechers seasons) may simply not write it.
ins.colourRow: {{ styles }} styles · {{ materials }} materials · {{ seasons }} seasons

aiSettings.title: AI connections
aiSettings.subtitle: Choose which AI service each job uses: Google's cloud (Gemini) today, the in-house AI server later. Changes apply within a minute, without restarting the server.
aiSettings.jobsHint: Each job uses one connection and model. Jobs left on the app default use the server's configuration file.

text.title: Text
text.what: AI Studio: smart search, change summaries, BOM check explanations, render descriptions. Concept Studio briefs, Cost Optimization ideas, Market Trends analysis. AI Lab: material reader, import fixes, concept matching, assistant.

embedding.title: Embedding
embedding.what: AI Lab: look-alike search (compares pictures and descriptions).

vision.title: Vision
vision.what: AI Lab: colour reader (reads colorway photos).

document.title: Document
document.what: AI Lab: tech pack reader (reads PDF pages).

prediction.title: Prediction
prediction.what: AI Lab: cost and lead-time forecasts (an in-house prediction service).

aiSettings.listModels: List the models this connection offers
aiSettings.modelRequired: Enter the model name the service uses.
aiSettings.noConnectionsHint: Add the in-house AI server (OpenAI-compatible: vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI) or a Gemini key, then point jobs at it.

kindHint.Gemini: Google's cloud AI. Needs an API key from Google AI Studio. Data sent leaves the LT network.
kindHint.OpenAiCompatible: Any server with an OpenAI-style API: vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio or LocalAI on the in-house AI server (address usually ends in /v1).
kindHint.Custom: Another HTTP service, e.g. an in-house prediction service for AI Lab. The app only checks that it answers.

aiSettings.deleteMessage: Delete the connection {{ name }}? Its saved API key is deleted too.
aiSettings.securityNote: API keys are encrypted before they are saved and never shown again; only their last 4 characters are displayed. Back up the server's App_Data/keys folder with the database, or saved keys must be entered again after a restore.
aiSettings.name: Name
aiSettings.keepKey: Saved key ends in {{ hint }}; leave blank to keep it
aiSettings.inHouseHint: Untick if this address is an outside service; AI pages then warn that data leaves LT.
aiSettings.geminiCloud: Gemini is always a cloud service.
aiSettings.notesPlaceholder: e.g. GPU server in the Phnom Penh data room; contact IT
aiSettings.jobOffHint: Turned off: this job makes no AI calls, not even to the app default.

blocked.aiOff: Not running: all AI is turned off
blocked.jobOff: Not running: this job is turned off
blocked.cloudBlocked: Blocked: its service is in the cloud and cloud AI is not allowed

switches.title: Switches
switches.hint: Apply to every AI feature, whatever the jobs below or the server's configuration file say. Changes apply to the next AI call.
switches.aiOn: On: AI features can run with the services set below.
switches.aiOff: Off: no AI call is made anywhere in the app. Features that need AI say so; everything else works.
switches.cloudOn: On: jobs may use services outside the LT network (Gemini, or connections not marked in-house). Data sent to them leaves LT.
switches.cloudOff: Off: only in-house services are used. Jobs set to a cloud service are blocked, so no data leaves LT.
switches.saved: Switches saved. They apply to the next AI call.

allowCloud.title: Allow cloud AI services?
allowCloud.message: Jobs set to a cloud service (such as Gemini) will start sending data outside LT: style and BOM details, concept briefs, and for Cost Optimization and Market Trends also prices and costs. See the AI documentation for exactly what each feature sends.

aiOff.title: Turn all AI features off?
aiOff.message: No AI call will be made anywhere in the app until AI is turned on again. Screens that need AI will say it is turned off.
